HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP — TERMLY EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Destroying road signs
   B. Littering in markets
   C. Obeying laws and caring for public property
   D. Avoiding all community work

2. Which statement about Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Say Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship never happens in Kenya.
   B. Treat Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship as rumours only.
   C. Explain Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Critical issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship.

3. A map key (legend) is used to: (1 mark)
   A. Name the president
   B. Explain symbols used on a map
   C. Measure rainfall only
   D. Replace the compass rose

4. Which statement about Political developments in independent Africa is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Skip evidence when discussing Political developments in independent Africa.

   C. Say Political developments in independent Africa never happens in Kenya.
   D. Treat Political developments in independent Africa as rumours only.

   A. Explain Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.
   B. Treat Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya as rumours only.
   C. Say Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya never happens in Kenya.
   D. Skip evidence when discussing Structure and functions of the county government of Kenya.

13. A budget helps a family to: (1 mark)
   A. Plan income and spending wisely
   B. Hide all money underground
   C. Avoid saving forever
   D. Ignore prices in shops

14. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
